hints: Because the speed is constant and the car's engine does no work, the loss in gravitational potential energy of the whole system must exactly equal the total work done against resistance forces.
The total mass of the car and trailer is $(m + 300)\text{ kg}$. In moving $50\text{ m}$ down the slope of $3^\circ$, the vertical distance descended is $h = 50\sin 3^\circ$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the loss in gravitational potential energy of the combined car and trailer system over $50\text{ m}$ down the $3^\circ$ slope:
$$\Delta PE = (m + 300)g(50\sin 3^\circ) = (m + 300)(10)(50\sin 3^\circ) = 500(m + 300)\sin 3^\circ$$

Equate the potential energy lost to the total work done against resistance forces ($40\,000\text{ J}$):
$$500(m + 300)\sin 3^\circ - 40\,000 = 0$$
$$500(m + 300)\sin 3^\circ = 40\,000$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the work-energy principle for the combined system of car and trailer:
$$\Delta KE + \Delta PE + W_{\text{resistance}} = W_{\text{engine}}$$
Identify the given conditions:
- Constant speed means kinetic energy does not change: $\Delta KE = 0$
- The engine is doing no work: $W_{\text{engine}} = 0$
Therefore, the potential energy lost while moving downhill is entirely converted into overcoming resistance:
$$\Delta PE_{\text{lost}} = W_{\text{resistance}}$$

Determine the potential energy lost in travelling $d = 50\text{ m}$ down the incline:
- Combined mass: $M = m + 300\text{ kg}$
- Vertical descent: $h = d\sin 3^\circ = 50\sin 3^\circ$
- Acceleration due to gravity: $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$
$$\Delta PE_{\text{lost}} = Mgh = (m + 300)(10)(50\sin 3^\circ) = 500(m + 300)\sin 3^\circ$$

Equate this expression to the given work done against resistance ($40\,000\text{ J}$):
$$500(m + 300)\sin 3^\circ = 40\,000$$

Subtract $300$ from both sides to find $m$:
$$m = 1528.60 - 300 = 1228.60\text{ kg}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $m = 1230\text{ kg}$.

hints: Isolate the trailer (mass $300\text{ kg}$) and resolve forces along the inclined plane.
Since the trailer moves at a constant speed, the acceleration is zero ($a = 0$), so the forces acting down the plane equal the forces acting up the plane.
Set up the equilibrium equation $T + 300g\sin 3^\circ - 200 = 0$ and solve for the tension $T$.
walkthrough:
Apply Newton's second law with $a = 0$ along the slope for the trailer:
$$T + 300g\sin 3^\circ - 200 = 0$$

Substitute $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and solve for tension $T$:
$$T = 200 - 300(10)\sin 3^\circ$$
$$T = 200 - 3000\sin 3^\circ = 200 - 156.987 = 43.0\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Identify all forces acting on the $300\text{ kg}$ trailer parallel to the inclined plane:
- Downward component of the trailer's weight: $W_{\parallel} = mg\sin 3^\circ = (300)(10)\sin 3^\circ = 3000\sin 3^\circ$
- Opposing resistance force up the slope: $R = 200\text{ N}$
- Tension $T$ in the tow-bar acting down the slope on the trailer

Since the motion is at constant speed, acceleration is zero ($a = 0$). By Newton's second law parallel to the plane:
$$\sum F_{\parallel} = ma$$
$$T + 300g\sin 3^\circ - 200 = 0$$

Rearrange to make $T$ the subject of the formula:
$$T = 200 - 3000\sin 3^\circ$$
Evaluate the trigonometric term:
$$3000\sin 3^\circ \approx 3000 \times 0.052336 = 156.987\text{ N}$$
Substitute and subtract:
$$T = 200 - 156.987 = 43.013\text{ N}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $T = 43.0\text{ N}$.
